slides.title: Recipes add shares
slides.text: The Bakery recipe book adds shares all day: half a cup of flour, then a fourth more. Adding fractions starts with one question: are the pieces the same size?

visual.label: The recipe book adds shares: half a cup of flour, then a fourth more

focus.cue: The recipe starts with 1/2 a cup of flour.
Then 1/4 more. Are the pieces the same size? Not yet.

slides.title: Same size pieces add
slides.text: When pieces match, adding is counting. Two eighths plus three eighths is five eighths: you count the pieces, and the piece size stays eighths.

visual.label: Adding eighths: 2/8 plus 3/8 is 5/8, the piece size stays eighths

focus.cue: The pieces match: both are eighths, so adding is counting.
Count the pieces: 2 + 3 = 5 eighths. The size stays eighths.

slides.title: Rough first, then re-slice
slides.text: Rough first: 1/2 + 1/4 lands between 1/2 and 1 whole. The pieces do not match, so re-slice the half first.
steps: 3/4 sits where our rough guess said

visual.label: Re-slice before adding: 1/2 becomes 2/4, then 2/4 plus 1/4 is 3/4

rows.label: 1/2: too big a piece to add to fourths

slides.title: The Jumble adds the bottoms
slides.text: The Jumble added 1/2 + 1/4 and wrote 2/6. It counted the pieces and the cuts. A mistake is a clue: the bottom number names the piece size, and sizes do not add.

slides.title: Stretch: Mixed numbers
slides.text: Big shares join in two piles. For 1 1/4 + 2 1/4, add the wholes (3), then the fourths (2/4), and the answer is 3 2/4.

visual.label: Adding mixed numbers: wholes, then fourths

focus.cue: Then the fourths: 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4. The answer is 3 2/4.

words.means: fractions whose pieces are the same size, ready to add
fractions whose pieces differ in size, needing a re-slice
a whole number and a fraction together, like 2 1/2
the total when amounts are added together

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Fraction Factory at Recipe Maths, then serve the orders. Re-slice until the pieces match before you add any two shares.
